title: What are these four products?
description: The video finds four products of two fractions by multiplying the tops and the bottoms, the same way as the example in the book, and reduces the answers that need it. It ends by checking the answers against the fractions.
teaching_notes: One idea: the tops multiply to give the shaded parts and the bottoms multiply to give all the parts. Watch for students who forget to reduce the answer to its simplest form.

video_script.why: The child has multiplied the tops and the bottoms for single products and now does it for four products, with some answers to reduce.
video_script.substitution: The tops multiply to give the shaded parts, and the bottoms multiply to give all the parts of the square.
video_script.anchor: Four products of two fractions, using a unit square as the whole
video_script.payoff_line: Four sixths times three fifths is twelve thirtieths, which is two fifths

final_answer.spoken: eight fifteenths, one sixth, three tenths and two fifths

video_script.fraction_reading: two thirds, four fifths, eight fifteenths, one quarter, one sixth, three fifths, one half, three tenths, four sixths, twelve thirtieths, two fifths
maths_rules: check: both fractions are below 1, so each product is smaller than both
video_script.design: One idea: the tops multiply and the bottoms multiply, then reduce. A unit square with shaded parts over all parts is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the products 2/3 × 4/5, 1/4 × 2/3, 3/5 × 1/2 and 4/6 × 3/5 written one under the other

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.four: the four products appear one under the other beside a unit square

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Find four products of two fractions, using a unit square as the whole.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a unit square cut into rows and columns; some small parts shaded; shaded parts over all parts

marks.sq: a unit square cut into rows and columns appears with some small parts shaded
marks.all: rows × columns = all the small parts is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sq'/>In a unit square, each product is the shaded parts counted over all the parts.
<bookmark mark='all'/>All the parts are the rows times the columns.

beats.on_screen: Given: 2/3 × 4/5, 1/4 × 2/3, 3/5 × 1/2 and 4/6 × 3/5, with a unit square as the whole

marks.given: the four products are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four products of two fractions, with a unit square as the whole.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each product

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the value of each product.

marks.a2: (2 × 4)/(3 × 5) is written with the tops and the bottoms marked

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Step one, take two thirds times four fifths.
Do it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Multiply the tops, two times four, and multiply the bottoms, three times five.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>That gives eight over fifteen.

marks.b2: the tops give 2 and the bottoms give 12, so 2/12 is written
marks.b3: 2/12 is divided by 2 on the top and the bottom to give 1/6

narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>Step two, take one quarter times two thirds.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>The tops give two, and the bottoms give twelve.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>Divide the top and the bottom by two to get one sixth.

marks.c2: the tops give 3 and the bottoms give 10, so 3/10 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, take three fifths times one half.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>The tops give three, and the bottoms give ten.

marks.d2: (4 × 3)/(6 × 5) is written with the tops and the bottoms marked

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step four, take four sixths times three fifths.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Multiply the tops, four times three, and multiply the bottoms, six times five.

beats.on_screen: Step 5 (check): both fractions in each product are below 1, so each answer must be smaller than both of them

marks.check: both fractions in each product are marked as below 1
marks.fits: each answer is marked as smaller than both of its fractions

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the products against the fractions.
Both fractions in each product are less than one.
<bookmark mark='fits'/>Each answer must be smaller than both of them.

marks.ans: the answers 8/15, 1/6 and 3/10 are written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first three products are eight fifteenths, one sixth and three tenths.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Four sixths times three fifths is twelve thirtieths, which is two fifths.
